summary: Today's news broke no holding's thesis. None of the 13 holdings has an 8-K, 10-Q or 10-K in the 7-day window, and none has a 4.01, 4.02, 5.02 or large 1.01/2.01. The day's single-name news was positive for held names: Baird upgraded DPZ to Outperform with a $400 PT (DPZ +2.3%), and Wells Fargo raised its WMT PT to $135 from $120, roughly the tenth raise before the print (WMT +1.2% after the one-third trim). The macro threads continued. Huang's resignation is now final, with Colette Kress as interim CEO, so the 11-12 report of succession planning has turned into fact four sessions before Nvidia's 11-17 print. BTC broke the $70K level that the 11-10 piece asked about and fell to about $69K, with more than $1B in liquidations. Gold fell below $4,000 to a one-year low. On the other side, Benzinga reports $37.5B of five-day US equity ETF inflows led by VOO and QQQ. Today's sales took VNQ and IEF out of the book. They had no fresh headlines; the only rates-tagged item is the 11-11 Thorne opinion piece. Per L2, I checked every held name's own earnings estimate and filings, not only the flagged ones.

memory_followups: QQQ/VOO/VTI: the Huang thread, which began 11-09 with the probe, went to reported succession planning on 11-12 and is now a confirmed resignation with Kress as interim CEO and Trump publicly naming Tim Cook. The Nasdaq 100 closed green on 11-12 despite NVDA's intraday drop of as much as 14.3%. The 11-12 high-risk flag rests on the dated 11-17 print, which has not happened yet. My QQQ flags graded mostly wrong at 5 days, so this is event risk, not a direction call.

BTC/ETH (shadow only, not held): the fourth leg down came true within a day. BTC went from $75K on 11-09 to $73K on 11-10 and 11-12, then to about $69K on 11-13, with ETF outflows, Iran comments and the Nvidia shock cited. There was no exchange failure; the FBI item on North Korean deepfake theft ($400M) concerns individual victims, not an exchange.
WMT: the open question from 11-10 to 11-12 is closed. The date is now company-confirmed, so the 'last year + 364 days' estimate turned out right.
DPZ: the Baird upgrade is the first rating change since the 10-30 guidance-cut rumor that came to nothing.

Not held: DBX filed a new 8-K on 11-12 (items 1.01, 2.03, 3.02, 8.01, 9.01), most likely the indenture for the $1.1B convertible priced on 11-10 (inference). FTDR filed a new 8-K 5.02 on 11-12 that can't be read from item numbers and has no explaining headline. MCO filed an 8-K 8.01 on 11-13, probably the euro notes (inference). EME's P1 Construction deal is small (about $600M-$650M of revenue against a market cap of about $29B), and there is no 8-K. CVS took a Deutsche downgrade to Neutral with a $104 PT, its third PT cut in four sessions, and Halper Sadeh has opened a fiduciary probe.
